title: Unit 1 rem early
english: Solomon says: “Will the one who rejoices over a person who is perishing go unpunished?” (Proverbs 17:5) Or perhaps wisdom rejoices the way she rejoiced over the ruin of Matthew the tax collector, and over the ruin of the robber who believed in Christ. In the one case wisdom destroyed the robber’s old life; in the other, the tax collector’s.

A “siege” is ethical teaching that tears down a soul badly built, under God’s siege. Just as infants stand between the just and the unjust, so all human beings stand between angels and demons—neither demons nor ranked as angels—until the completion of the age. He said they were wronging “infants,” of whom Christ said, “Do not cause one of these little ones to stumble.” (Matthew 18:6) The person free from passion rests without fear from every evil thought, and soon will lodge in the kingdom of God, because he heard and kept God’s commands and hoped in him.

In this way a person hides God’s command by doing it, or by doing it not for empty glory. That is why the demons, by not letting us do it, are said to snatch it away. Then you will understand how the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and how it becomes the broker of the knowledge of God—when in faith and longing you come to him as one in need. Wisdom and understanding must be there first if someone is to grasp the fear of the Lord. Bring this home to those who despise wisdom and understanding, yet want to take refuge in fearing God as if it were an easy thing.

If Christ does not rescue us, we will travel the bad road as if it were good. Holy people say all things that are faithful—but not everything is. The devil has nothing faithful, nothing worthy of trust. Here “man” means the devil, as in the Gospels, if a wicked man sowed the weeds (Matthew 13:25-28). The greatest plot, it seems, is to fall in with a bad counsel and with crafty, insidious, wicked men. If that kind of counsel—crushed, that is, darkened—is a motion of the mind, how did it abandon the teaching of youth? How did it forget the divine covenant? He speaks to us of bad counsel as of a rational living being.

Or here “bad counsel” means the devil. For he counseled badly when he said, “I will set my throne above the stars, and I will be like the Most High.” (Isaiah 14:13-14) He forgot the divine knowledge when he left the teaching of youth—and that “youth” shows his former state, in which he was also zealous. If she can make the young understanding where so much is hard to rein in when she is absent, she is far more useful to an elder. Those who are overtaken by years of life through the works of the coming ever-living life seize the straight paths of an untroubled and unbroken life. They are not overtaken by his compassions into the paths of that straight everlasting life.

For the Lord loves those who pursue righteousness, and the counsel of the evil one will not overtake them. But those who trust the devil do not seize the straight paths of life, nor will they turn back into the kingdom of God. The one who does not live lawfully forgets the law; the one who lives by it remembers it. The one who keeps God’s words is not only the one who does them, but also the one who advises others. The one who loses them is the one who will not practice them and who hinders others. For it is not the hearers of the law who will be justified (Romans 2:13).

Healing is the health that comes from virtue for your way of life; God’s grace and care belong to your thoughts and intentions. When the soul’s powers—that is, the virtues—receive care, then all my bones will say, “Lord, Lord, who is like you?” (Psalm 35:10) The memorial power of the soul, once it receives care, will surely say, “I remembered God and was glad.” (Psalm 77:3) Likewise the seeing power will say, “I considered your works and was amazed.” (Habakkuk 3:2) So too the desiring power: “Lord, before you is all my desire.” (Psalm 38:9) And the rational power: “I reasoned through the ancient days.” (Psalm 77:5) The same will follow for the other powers.

That is: for those who are willing, nothing is hard—not like the desire for money. A pure mind draws near to wisdom, because it knows the good; the unclean mind will be far from her. After the transgression Adam is forbidden to partake of this tree—if a tree of life is planted from the fruits of righteousness. And the tree of life is the wisdom of God. added_allusions.reason: The lemma under exposition is quoted at the head of the section: "Will the one who rejoices over a person who is perishing go unpunished?" is Proverbs 17:5 (ὁ ἐπιχαίρων ἀπολλυμένῳ οὐκ ἀθῳωθήσεται). Recorded ref (recorded form "Prov 17:5"), checked and reused.
Christ's saying is quoted: Μὴ σκανδαλίσητε ἕνα τῶν μικρῶν τούτων, "Do not cause one of these little ones to stumble". Recorded ref (recorded form "Matt 18:6"), checked and reused.

"Here 'man' means the devil, as in the Gospels, if a wicked man sowed the weeds": the parable's enemy who sowed ζιζάνια among the wheat (Matthew 13:25) and is named ἐχθρὸς ἄνθρωπος, "an enemy, a man" (13:28). Missed reference, verified against the Greek.

The devil's counsel is quoted in his own words: «Ἐπάνω τῶν ἄστρων θήσω τὸν θρόνον μου, καὶ ἔσομαι ὅμοιος τῷ Ὑψίστῳ», "I will set my throne above the stars, and I will be like the Most High". Recorded ref (recorded form "Isa 14:13-14"), checked and reused.

"For it is not the hearers of the law who will be justified" restates Romans 2:13 (οὐ γὰρ οἱ ἀκροαταὶ νόμου δίκαιοι παρὰ τῷ θεῷ, ἀλλ' οἱ ποιηταὶ νόμου δικαιωθήσονται). Recorded ref (recorded form "Rom 2:13"), checked and reused.

The bones' saying «Κύριε, Κύριε, τίς ὅμοιός σοι;», "Lord, Lord, who is like you?", is Psalm 35:10 (LXX 34:10: πάντα τὰ ὀστᾶ μου ἐροῦσιν, Κύριε, τίς ὅμοιός σοι). Recorded ref (recorded form "Ps 35:10"), checked and reused.
The memory power's saying «Ἐμνήσθην τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ εὐφράνθην», "I remembered God and was glad", is Psalm 77:3 (LXX 76:4). Missed reference, verified against the Greek.
The seeing power's saying, "I considered your works and was amazed" (κατενόησα τὰ ἔργα σου καὶ ἐξέστην), is Habakkuk 3:2. Missed reference, verified against the Greek.
The desiring power's saying «Κύριε, ἐναντίον σου πᾶσα ἡ ἐπιθυμία μου», "Lord, before you is all my desire", is Psalm 38:9 (LXX 37:10). Missed reference, verified against the Greek.
The rational power's saying «Διελογισάμην ἡμέρας ἀρχαίας», "I reasoned through the ancient days", is Psalm 77:5 (LXX 76:6). Missed reference, verified against the Greek.

title: Unit 1 rem mid
english: and the clouds ran with dews (Proverbs 3:19-20). So the “earth” he named here, holy Paul called breadth; and what are called heavens here, Paul in Ephesians calls height; and the abysses named in a figure he calls depth; the dewed clouds he calls length (Ephesians 3:18). All of these are symbols of rational natures, divided among worlds and body according to the analogy of their state. This also fits the Son of God now. But the faithful soul is also earth that bears a hundredfold (Matthew 13:8). From the richness that is wisdom she becomes wise, while God founds her upon it. For he settles the gathering of teaching and makes a fastening from wisdom. And as she always advances, he makes her heaven—a purest creature, a dwelling of angels and of noetic essences—once she has received sense of what is and contemplates the exactness of things, as if the many-storied judgments of God.

Against wisdom alone the demons are powerless. They are not allowed to cast thoughts into the heart of the one who has been made wise. For the mind that competes for the contemplations of wisdom becomes unreceptive of unclean thoughts. A pure mind draws near to wisdom, because it knows the good; the unclean mind will be far from her. A stumbling-block for a rational nature is an unclean thought or false knowledge. But the one fenced round by God’s counsel does not stumble in these things.

Neither an assault of wicked thoughts, he says, will frighten the one who has become wise, nor will the impious who attack from outside tear down his power when they want to strip him of natural goods. No one can take what cannot be captured—and what is more arrogant than the impious person? Yet you will also overcome that many-formed beast if you are gentle and equitable, while the Lord is with you. From this we learn that mercy removes the fearful phantasms that meet us by night, or also in contemplation. And not only that: it also removes from those who think this way the wicked accusations at the departure and the harmful chastisements in the judgment. Gentleness, freedom from anger, long-suffering, and whatever naturally settles stirred wrath do the same—if fearful appearances usually arise from the turmoil of wrath.

Do not hold back from doing good not only with food for the needy, but also with the knowledge of God, with wisdom, and with the commandments. And whatever is dear to God and joins a person to him, do not hold back from doing that good to the one who needs you. This enmity toward the neighbor makes someone evil not only in body but also in soul. Ignorance of the Lord is in the houses of the impious, but knowledge of God is in the souls of the just. The dwellings of the just are blessed when Christ apportions the prizes to each according to their works; to the impious he apportions a curse and not a blessing.

Extreme vice raised to its end is called pride. The Lord arrays himself against the unjust as righteousness, against liars as truth, against the proud as humility. That is why he is a friend to those who think humble thoughts—for that is what “He gives grace to the humble” means—and against the proud he arrays himself (Proverbs 3:34). Those who have learned and taught godly wisdom will inherit heavenly glory. The impious raised dishonor for themselves before angels and human beings from Christ.

By “training” he means ethical virtue; by “thought,” divine knowledge. A “son of the virtues” is the one qualified according to them, who acts not for someone else’s sake but for virtue’s sake in what accords with it. “I grant you a good gift, the heavenly kingdom, if you do not abandon my law.” Note here that he names the mind a good gift, because of the one who takes gifts unjustly in the bosom and is not prospered (Proverbs 17:23). Those unjust gifts mean the affairs of the evil one; when the mind receives them, it is not prospered in its ways.

A crown of graces are God’s commandments, which give back the crown of the kingdom to those who do them. A crown of delight is the knowledge of God, which shields us and thrusts away every passionate thought and every false knowledge. These many ways lead into one way—the one who said, “I am the way.” (John 14:6) He called many ways the virtues that carry a person to the knowledge of God. The years of life of the one who hears through the prophets of the heavenly Father will be multiplied, and who receives his words through the only-begotten Son, so as to be directed in the ways of righteousness of life and saved into the ever-living life. added_allusions.reason: The clause that closes the previous section and opens this one, "God founded the earth by wisdom; and through his sense the abysses were broken open, and the clouds ran with dews", is Proverbs 3:19-20 in near-verbatim form. The citation sits where the clause ends, at the head of this section. Missed reference, verified against the English and the sense of the Greek.

The section itself names the source: what are called earth, heavens, and abysses here, "Paul in Ephesians calls" breadth, height, depth, and length, which is the fourfold measure of Ephesians 3:18. Recorded ref (recorded form "Eph 3:18"), checked and reused.
"The faithful soul is also earth that bears a hundredfold" takes up the sower parable's yield, ὃ δὴ ἑκατόν (Matthew 13:8; also 13:23). Missed reference, verified against the Greek.
"The one who takes gifts unjustly in the bosom and is not prospered" restates Proverbs 17:23 (δῶρα ὁ λαμβάνων ἐν κόλπῳ ἀδίκως οὐ κατευθύνεται). Missed reference, verified against the Greek.

"He gives grace to the humble, and against the proud he arrays himself" is Proverbs 3:34 (LXX: Κύριος ὑπερηφάνοις ἀντιτάσσεται, ταπεινοῖς δὲ δίδωσιν χάριν), the verse James 4:6 repeats. Added as clear on the same clause where the recorded James reference was demoted. Missed reference found by the check and verified against the Greek.

Recorded ref (recorded form "Jas 4:6"). Demoted to possible: the wording on this clause is Proverbs 3:34, which James 4:6 itself quotes; James is the repeater, not the source of the wording. Proverbs 3:34 carries the inline instead. Not inlined.
"The one who said, 'I am the way'" (Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ὁδός) quotes John 14:6 directly. Recorded ref, checked and reused.

title: Unit 1 rem close
english: The place of the army is wickedness and false knowledge, and everything unacceptable to God. For the impious reasonings are enemies, killing souls. In his beloved ones the Lord gives sleep (Psalm 127:2), but the impious are not his beloved ones, therefore to the impious the Lord does not give sleep. Hence it can also be persuasively shown that they are not by nature sleepers, the demons. Our virtues go before us and enlighten us in the present life, which is called night in relation to the coming day. Until the day is established in which the sun of righteousness rises (Malachi 4:2). Or, until they establish us in safety, they do not depart, for this is characteristic of day, to disperse darkness. Which also Christ said: The one walking in the day does not stumble (John 11:9). On the contrary, the reasonings of the impious, since they did not know nor understand, wander in darkness (Psalm 82:5). They stumble, but they do not have indulgence as those stumbling through ignorance, for they themselves have worked darkness. See how virtue even in darkness produced light, and wickedness even in light produced darkness. Neither the manner in which they sin do the impious know, nor do they know the cause, whence they stumble. But they do not even know this, that they transgress, which is a sign of the utmost wickedness. He calls the virtues springs, from which flows the living water of the divine words, which is the knowledge of Christ. And David: They appeared, he says, the springs of the waters, and the foundations of the world were uncovered (Psalm 18:15), evidently by the visitation of our Savior Jesus Christ. Your eyes, he said, look straight ahead. This is the things which alone are dear to God, or the things made clear to us by the prophets concerning Christ alone and his disciples. And all things spoken by someone toward Christ, befitting him, and only him. This agrees with: Unless the Lord builds the house and guards the city (Psalm 127:1), that is, unless the Lord gives us strength to direct the steps toward him, we labor in vain, we who do not call upon him in comfort, but undertake in arrogance. For the conspicuous prostitutes and the teachings of the heterodox deceive the innocent hearts through flattery (Romans 16:18). Therefore the greatest safety is not to take hold of the beginning, for having taken hold, it is difficult to escape. As far as their hearing, it is good. But the fat signifies the pleasure from which impurity is born, whose offspring, wickedness and ignorance. Of which nothing more bitter can be found in the events of the day of judgment. Hence we know that the spirited part dominates in the demons, for he says, unmerciful is the spirit, and their anger is sharp. For they hunt for destruction those who obey them, thus they honor those who honor them. Through wickedness the evil ones wear away the flesh of Christ, and they consume the blood, having considered it common. For he says, the one eating my flesh and drinking my blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day (John 6:53-56). But the one eating unworthily the body and drinking the blood of the Lord, eats and drinks judgment to himself (1 Corinthians 11:27-29). There was when there was no evil, and there will be when there will be no evil. For the seeds of virtue are inexhaustible. And this convinces me a little, and not yet completely in every evil having become, the rich one in Hades being judged by wickedness, and having pity on the brothers. And to pity, it obtains the finest seed of virtue. Knowledge and a spring is a well. For those who approach the virtues, it is considered to be a deep well. But to the apathetic and pure, a spring. Thus also the Savior sat by the well, the hour was about the sixth (John 4:6). Consider the well the divine knowledge, and not the well of water. Just as the spring is ready as it were, that is, the flowing water to the thirsty, so the well in labor to those who wish to draw. And just as the spring is unfailing in flowing, so the sensory writing has an unceasing course, and it is easy for the thirsty to grow old in God. And just as the well provides labor to those who draw, so the theoretical knowledge to those who wish through it to accomplish the virtues, of soul and body, to contemplate the divine things, and to counterfeit the kingdom of heaven. A woman here signifies the knowledge of God. This was given to us from youth. Whom Solomon in his youth teaching says, Son, lest an evil counsel seize you, speaking of the devil, as having counseled evil. She who has abandoned teaching.

added_allusions.reason: "In his beloved ones the Lord gives sleep" restates Psalm 127:2 (ὅταν δῷ τοῖς ἀγαπητοῖς αὐτοῦ ὕπνον). Missed reference, verified against the Greek (ἀγαπητοῖς and ὕπνον both present).
"Until the day is established in which the sun of righteousness rises": the sun of righteousness is Malachi 4:2 (LXX 3:20, ἥλιος δικαιοσύνης). Recorded ref, checked and reused.
Introduced as Christ's own saying: «Ὁ περιπατῶν ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ οὐ προσκόπτει», "The one walking in the day does not stumble", is John 11:9. Missed reference, verified against the Greek.
"Since they did not know nor understand, they wander in darkness" restates Psalm 82:5 (LXX 81:5: οὐκ ἔγνωσαν οὐδὲ συνῆκαν, ἐν σκότει διαπορεύονται). Missed reference, verified against the Greek.

Introduced as David's words: "the springs of the waters appeared, and the foundations of the world were uncovered" (ὤφθησαν αἱ πηγαὶ τῶν ὑδάτων, καὶ ἀνεκαλύφθησαν τὰ θεμέλια τῆς οἰκουμένης) is Psalm 18:15 (LXX 17:16). Missed reference, verified against the Greek.
"Unless the Lord builds the house and guards the city, we labor in vain" is Psalm 127:1, quoted and then glossed. Recorded ref, checked and reused.

"The teachings of the heterodox deceive the innocent hearts through flattery" restates Romans 16:18: by smooth talk and flattery they deceive the hearts of the innocent (ἐξαπατῶσιν τὰς καρδίας τῶν ἀκάκων). Missed reference, verified against the Greek.

Introduced as the Lord's saying: "the one eating my flesh and drinking my blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day" is John 6:54, inside the recorded range. Recorded ref, checked and reused.

"The one eating unworthily the body and drinking the blood of the Lord eats and drinks judgment to himself" joins 1 Corinthians 11:27 (eating and drinking unworthily, ἀναξίως) with 11:29 (κρῖμα ἑαυτῷ ἐσθίει καὶ πίνει). Missed reference, verified against the Greek.

"The Savior sat by the well, the hour was about the sixth" carries the three narrative markers of John 4:6: Jesus seated at the well (ἐκαθέζετο ἐπὶ τῇ πηγῇ) at about the sixth hour. This is a separate, narrative reference; it does not revive the demoted living water entry. Missed reference, verified against the Greek.

Recorded ref. Demoted to possible: the clause turns on the two-word phrase "living water" (ὕδωρ ζῶν), and John 7:38 (rivers of living water) is an equal rival for the springs and flowing water language of this section. Not inlined.
